headline: Rays rout Phillies 12-1 as skid reaches four games
recap: The Phillies' losing streak reached four games in a 12-1 rout by the Tampa Bay Rays at Citizens Bank Park. Junior Caminero opened the scoring with a two-run homer in the first inning, and Richie Palacios followed with an RBI double to make it 3-0. Aaron Nola was charged with the loss after allowing all three of those runs in just one inning of work. Tampa Bay broke it open with four more runs in the fifth, capped by a two-run single from Cedric Mullins, then added three more in the sixth on run-scoring hits from Victor Mesa Jr. and Palacios. Philadelphia's only run came in the seventh, when Bryson Stott scored on a fielding error by Rays second baseman Richie Palacios. The Rays tacked on two final runs in the ninth on a Ryan Vilade single. Bryson Stott went 2-for-4 with two doubles, and Trea Turner had a double and a single.

The loss leaves Philadelphia at 87-74, seven games behind the first-place Atlanta Braves in the NL East. The Phillies still hold the third and final National League Wild Card spot, but the four-game skid has pulled the Arizona Diamondbacks to within one game in that race.

Philadelphia is back home this afternoon to close out the three-game series against Tampa Bay, with first pitch at Citizens Bank Park set for 3:05 p.m. ET. Zack Wheeler is scheduled to start for the Phillies opposite Nick Martinez for the Rays. Philadelphia is a -149 favorite on the moneyline.
